### T-084 — `core/blong-lint`'s `ci-test` exits 1 because it has no tests

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-lint · open_

`core/blong-lint`'s `ci-test` exits 1 because the package has no test files. That is pre-existing —
the old `blong-dev test` did the same — and either adding tests or dropping the script and letting
rush's `ignoreMissingScript: true` skip it would settle it.

### T-143 — A lint run that skips a tool must not look like a pass

> _2026-09-24 · core/blong-lint · open_

Make a lint run say what it did not check. Two silent gaps, one cause: `lintCollect` gates tsc and
eslint on the current working directory (`hasTsConfig(cwd)`, `hasEslintConfig(cwd)`) and prints only
the tools that ran, so a run from the repository root checks spelling and markdown, exits 0, and
looks like a pass; and ten packages ship no eslint config at all (core/blong-allure, core/blong-mle,
core/blong-template, core/config-hot-reload, realm/blong-access, realm/blong-access-mock,
realm/blong-core, realm/blong-gateway, demo/handler-test-poc, tools/blong-dev), so their ci-lint
never runs eslint either. Discover the tools from the packages the named files belong to, or print a
line naming the skipped tools and why; then decide whether the ten packages get the two-line config
that the others point at `tools/eslint/config.mjs` with, which will surface whatever eslint has been
missing there. See the friction on the file-scoped run that hid two type errors in a file I had just
edited.
